text:
alexa: FYI seeing p50/p95 spikes for intra-cluster RPCs between gpu-pool/* and inference-prod/*, started ~11:03 UTC. tcpdump shows a lot of SYN retransmits. Any recent NetworkPolicy or namespace isolation changes?

pranay: looking. I rolled out a namespace-level policy to harden gpu-pool earlier today (label isolation=yes). It was supposed to block external egress, but I’ll check the exact YAML.

santiago: I merged a sec-hardening chart last night that adds an egress-default-deny for labeled namespaces. Might be related.

alexa: quick tcpdump excerpt from node-12 shows packets reaching the pod IP but getting immediate RST/ICMP responses:
```
12:05:02.123456 IP 10.244.1.12.34912 > 10.244.2.8.9300: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 65535, options [mss 8952], length 0
12:05:02.223456 IP 10.244.2.8.9300 > 10.244.1.12.34912: RST, seq 0, win 0, length 0
```

meera: Are SR-IOV / RDMA-enabled pods affected? Some GPU nodes use SR-IOV and bypass parts of the CNI. NP is enforced at CNI level though. That MSS (8952) looks like jumbo frames – could be MTU differences too.

pranay: I found the exact NP that was applied to gpu-pool. It’s pretty minimal and I messed up the intent:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-isolation
  namespace: gpu-pool
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```

alexa: Yikes — egress: [] is an explicit deny-all egress for every pod in gpu-pool. That will block clusterIP traffic to pods in other namespaces unless you add allow rules.

santiago: Ugh, that was meant to block internet egress only, not east-west. The chart author (me) scoped it by namespace label but forgot to add allowed destinations for internal namespaces. My bad.

alexa: Can we patch it to allow traffic to inference-prod? Something like adding a to: with namespaceSelector for inference-prod.

pranay: Patch applied to allow namespaceSelector matchLabels: app: inference-prod and also allowed kube-dns. Rolling update now.

infra-bot: patch applied by pranay — networkpolicy patched in gpu-pool

alexa: p95 back to normal in ~40s after the patch. p95 dropped from ~320ms -> ~18ms. Looks clear.

meera: For follow-up: we should add an automated e2e connectivity test in the NetworkPolicy CI step that validates ClusterIP/DNS reachability between labeled namespaces before promoting policies to prod. Also document SR-IOV / RDMA interaction and MTU expectations.

santiago: Agree. I’ll add a canary policy deploy that runs a small curl/latency check between a test pod in gpu-pool and inference-prod.

pranay: Note for runbook: avoid using empty egress list for deny unless you explicitly add allow rules. Prefer deny with explicit to: entries or use annotations to indicate intended scope. Also call out special network types (SR-IOV) in the policy docs.

alexa: tagging networking and oncall for visibility: @networking @oncall :thumbsup:
